articles.title: LeBron James’s 76ers beat NY Knicks on NBA’s opening night at MSG
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers defeated NBA champions New York Knicks 106-100 as the new NBA season tipped off.
articles.body:
LeBron James and his new Philadelphia 76ers teammates crashed the New York Knicks’ season-opening celebrations, beating the defending NBA champions 106-100 on the night they raised their title banner at Madison Square Garden.

James, 41 and entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, scored 14 points and handed out seven of the 76ers’ 28 assists on Tuesday.

It was a tantalising glimpse of how he will be a facilitator for younger teammates like Tyrese Maxey – who led all scorers with 28 points.

“I could be a lot better,” James told a United States broadcaster NBC. “Still getting my rhythm, obviously just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad.

“But I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively.”

Jaylen Brown, the former Boston Celtics star who arrived in Philly in a stunning trade for Paul George in July, scored 19 points with eight rebounds and six assists and centre Joel Embiid added 13 points and 11 rebounds for the 76ers.

Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 21 points and Karl-Anthony Towns scored 19 points with 12 rebounds, but after regaining the lead in the third quarter, the 76ers repelled every Knicks charge.

The Knicks ended a 53-year title drought with their victory over the San Antonio Spurs in last season’s NBA Finals.

Knicks legends including Bill Bradley, Earl Monroe and Walt Frazier handed out the Knicks’ championship rings in an emotional pre-game ceremony at the Garden, where the crowd featured die-hard celebrity Knicks fans like Ben Stiller and Spike Lee, along with other famous faces including rocker Jon Bon Jovi and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.

Before the club’s third championship banner was raised to the rafters, NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Brunson told fans the Knicks were “ready to turn the page as a team”.

“But one thing I would like to say – the joy that this city had this summer we’d love to replicate that again,” Brunson said of a Knicks team aiming to be the first repeat champions since 2018.

James, a four-time NBA champion and the league’s all-time leading scorer, admitted that winning on another team’s ring ceremony night was especially satisfying.

In the nightcap of the opening day triple-header, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder rode a hot start to a 116-104 victory over Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs.

Wembanyama, widely tipped to end Gilgeous-Alexander’s two-year Most Valuable Player reign, made just one basket in 13 attempts, an alley-oop dunk to end the third quarter.

He made his presence felt with 13 rebounds and six blocked shots and scored 12 points, largely thanks to 10 free throws.

But the Spurs, led by 24 points from Stephon Castle, ultimately had no answer for an OKC outfit “hungry” after their title defence ended in a seven-game loss to San Antonio in last season’s Western Conference finals.

“Obviously this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “But for us, I think it was more like we’re just happy to be back. It’s a longer summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.”

There was plenty of tension between the young teams tipped to duel for supremacy in the West for years to come.

Spurs guard De’Aaron Fox was whistled for a flagrant foul after throwing Thunder centre Chet Holmgren to the court early in the second quarter, prompting a shoving match that resulted in multiple technical fouls.

The Spurs made a disciplined start to the third quarter and twice got the deficit to seven in the second half, only for the Thunder to pull away again.

The NBA’s 81st season tipped off in Detroit, where the Pistons used a fierce second-half fightback to spoil George’s 38-point Celtics debut in a duel of last season’s top two regular-season teams.

Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren scored 22 points each, and Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 in the fourth quarter as the Pistons rallied for a 121-113 victory with the aid of a 23-0 scoring run.

articles.title: Aday Mara: "Me hace gracia porque había gente que decía que no iba a jugar"
articles.standfirst: El español, feliz, habla de su debut en la NBA con los Oklahoma City Thunder
articles.summary: El español, feliz, habla de su debut en la NBA con los Oklahoma City Thunder
articles.body: El primer partido en la NBA es inolvidable. Eso le va a pasar a Aday Mara, que vivió un momento del que sólo unos pocos elegidos pueden presumir. Ya es jugador de la NBA tras debutar con los Oklahoma City Thunder. Pero es que además, el jugador español lo hizo a lo grande, con una convincente actuación, sobreponiéndose a la presión del ambiente y con un taponazo a Wembanyama que ha dado la vuelta al mundo. Fueron 12 minutos que ya son historia del baloncesto español. Al final del partido, en la sonrisa de Mara, se podía ver que estaba satisfecho de su rendimiento y feliz por su debut. Y se acordó de aquellos que vaticinaron que no jugaría este año en la NBA: "Estoy contento de que ya es oficial. Me hace gracia porque parecía que no iba a jugar, había gente por ahí que decía que no iba a jugar, así que otra cosa que va bien", recordaba Mara en declaraciones a Aragón Deporte tras el partido. Mara jugó 12 minutos anotando 7 puntos, además de coger 2 rebotes, dar una asistencias y poner un brutal tapón a 'Wemby': "Me he sentido bien jugando y he sentido que he ayudado al equipo, así que contento. Ha sido emotivo porque mis compañeros me han dado la bola, yo no lo había pensado. Eso me lo voy a quedar como recuerdo que es muy bonito", dijo. El coloso español recordaba para Aragon Deporte la jugada con la que ha derribado la puerta de la NBA: "La primera jugada que hago como un aro pasado, había pensado en hacer un mate, pero estaba mirando cómo era todo. Lo veo ahí y al final, como lo he visto tantas veces, lo ves jugar y más o menos te aprendes cómo él juega. O saltaba ahí antes, o hacía un mate, así que probé", relataba en referencia al tapón a Wembanyama en el tercer cuarto del partido. Al final del choque se produjo el momento más emotivo para Aday: acercarse a la grada y celebrar su debut y el triunfo con su fanilia: "Tener a mis padres aquí, que es el cumpleaños de mi padre hoy, ha sido muy bonito que ellos puedan estar, celebrar el cumple de mi padre con él y con mi madre y que hayan podido venir a ver el partido". Sobre la actuación del jugador aragonés, su entrenador Mark Daigneault fue muy claro al final del choque en San Antonio: "Ha tenido un gran impacto. Probablemente tuvo uno de los tramos del partido que fue decisivo. No pareció abrumado por el ambiente del partido. No me sorprende por su rendimiento en la pretemporada. Creo que ha demostrado ser un jugador de gran impacto. Esta noche no tuvo muchos minutos, pero su impacto fue notable Voy a confiar aún más en él después de ver cómo rindió en un partido de tan alto nivel".

articles.title: Inflation and borrowing data illustrate chancellor's Budget challenge
articles.summary: The economic figures released on Wednesday show the constraints for John Healey as he puts the finishing touches to his Budget.
articles.body:
The chancellor was on an early flight to North East Scotland on Wednesday to announce new North Sea energy approvals as the last set of major economic figures dropped.

From a mile high, as well as close up, the figures for inflation and for the public finances set out his Budget balancing act in clear terms.

The National Debt has topped £3 trillion for the first time in the official figures.

The headline rate of inflation has hit 3.5% and is surely heading back up to 4% in the coming months.

Borrowing is running ahead of forecasts, as spending and interest costs increase.

These show the constraints for John Healey as he puts the finishing touches to his statement next week.

On the one hand he says he wants to give "breathing space" to consumers yet again feeling the heat from cost of living pressures.

The public finances remain under pressure, however, from the double whammy of rising inflation and borrowing costs.

While inflation was of course expected to increase as petrol and diesel prices surged, in some cases, to records, other measures of underlying inflation also increased.

From airfares to computer game download prices, there are the first signs of stickier forms of price pressure and of higher inflation becoming more embedded, suggesting elevated price rises are not temporary. Capital Economics now expects the main measure of inflation to peak at 4.2% next year.

The Bank of England carefully watches services inflation and core inflation, and this ups the odds significantly for a rise in interest rates next month.

The services sector, which includes everything from law and banking to retail, hospitality and tourism, makes up the vast majority of the UK's economic output.

The latest inflation figure also applies as the uprating to tens of billions in welfare payments next April.

By law, benefits such as personal independence payment (PIP) and carer's allowance must rise in line with September's consumer price index (CPI) measure of inflation.

The figure also confirms that the Triple Lock will see the State Pension increase by 3.9% next April.

There is one form of relief here - food price inflation remains largely unaffected by the energy shock.

While higher inflation at a time of frozen tax thresholds will raise more tax in cash terms, it will also increase the cost of public services, including likely union pay demands.

All the while, UK borrowing costs have risen alongside most of the advanced world as the US-Israel war against Iran has intensified.

The Jackdaw gas field decision is seen as the start of a run of "pro growth" pre-Budget announcements.

It sends a directional message, but will not fundamentally change the trade off between cost of living breathing space, and delivering a Budget that convinces the markets and investors.

The fact the borrowing costs gap has narrowed a bit with other G7 nations, and the IMF praised pencilled-in plans to shrink borrowing, provided a platform for the chancellor's Budget.

The latest economic numbers amply illustrate the challenge of actually delivering them.

articles.title: The NBA star helping protect his opponents’ feet
articles.summary: NBA star Damian Lillard co-founded an insoles company. It turns out his biggest competition on the court are wearing them.
articles.body: Even before they even stepped out onto an NBA court as teammates, Portland Trail Blazers point guard Damian Lillard dished out an assist to his backcourt mate Ja Morant. At the start of the team’s preseason training camp, Morant was getting ready to put on his shoes when he mentioned to Lillard that he needed more pairs of the orthotics he was using. “You know that’s my company, right?” Lillard said to Morant, who initially thought Lillard was joking. Lillard hasn’t gone around the NBA evangelizing his own product, but as Morant’s usage showed, it turns out he hasn’t needed to. Move Insoles, the company Lillard co-founded with longtime athlete marketer Nate Jones, has already been widely adopted by athletes across multiple sports. Jones, who works at Goodwin Sports, the agency that represents Lillard, began working on Move in earnest in 2019. He courted Lillard as a co-founder, and other NBA stars such as Chris Paul and Jamal Crawford as investors. Jones estimates that around 25 NBA teams now use the product, in addition to non-basketball stars such as the Dallas Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb and five-time WNBA MVP A’Ja Wilson. And like Morant, those teams and players are using the insoles not because of a corporate partnership or at Lillard’s request, but through word of mouth. “I’ve been watching the NBA and been an NBA junkie my entire life,” said Jones. “So to create something that these players rely on, believe in, that their medical staffs rely on and believe in, is a big deal.” Lillard was eager to be an active participant in the company due to his own experiences. He’s been using orthotics in his shoes ever since college to help recover from a broken foot he suffered while at Weber State. Early in his NBA career, Lillard also dealt with plantar fasciitis, but he couldn’t find the right insole that was both comfortable and not a hindrance to his performance. “Needing more support in my shoe, especially having flat feet and the amount of miles on my feet, I understood the importance of not only having support in your shoe, but the right type of support and different options for different people,” said Lillard. The star guard hasn’t simply slapped his name on Move, he’s also made himself an integral part of the product development. Lillard has personally tested each of the four insoles Move sells, which range from a more comfort-oriented orthotic to more performance-oriented ones. While practicing with Team USA ahead of the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, Lillard was testing prototypes and giving feedback to Jones. “Me being somebody that’s going to be on the floor, somebody that’s had these [foot] issues that I mentioned, and also having real friendships with the people that I’m partnering with, they know I’m gonna tell the truth,” said Lillard. Jones said the biggest advantage of working with Lillard was his honesty, saying Lillard “won’t sugarcoat it” when it comes to his opinions. Now, not only is it common for Lillard to see other players wearing his signature shoe on the court, after games he’ll see players pulling out the insole he tested years earlier. Over the last year, as he missed all of the 2025-26 season with a torn Achilles, Lillard had extra time to devote to his business interests. “At this stage of my career and having that much time, I’m thinking about, ‘What do I see for my kids, and how do I want to try to help them more? What about when I’m not playing? What do I want to spend my time doing?’” Lillard said. He added that working on Move reaffirmed his interest in business opportunities that allow him to be involved from the ground up. Lillard and Jones still have further goals for their insoles, though, including targeting the youth sports market so athletes are aware of their foot health at a younger age. Move is also announcing soon it will be an official partner of the National Basketball Athletic Trainers Association, which means it’s even more likely some of Lillard’s opponents will have him to thank for helping their feet. Just don’t expect Lillard to be aggressively pitching the product now that he’s ready to resume his NBA career. He laughed when asked if he’s considered trying to find an investment on the TV show “Shark Tank.” “I‘ve watched the show, and I’ve had thoughts,” Lillard admitted. “It would be a hard show for me personally to be on, just because I would want to be prepared 1,000%. I wouldn’t want to have the responsibility of still being an active player.” For now, that means Lillard will have to settle for advertising by what he does on the court.
