articles.title: Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season
articles.summary: In here, it's always NBA trade season.
articles.body:
Regular-season basketball only just returned, but front offices are constantly projecting forward. Why should we be any different? And so, we ring in the New 82-Game Year with our first trade-target big board of the 2026-27 campaign.

Each mini list is built while accounting for team needs, directions, cap sheets and available assets. Names who aren't trade-eligible until December (or January) are fair game for this exercise. We will denote when players are able to be moved wherever necessary.

Every team will be given at least one ambitious target to keep things fun. Ultra-ambitious targets will be sprinkled in whenever appropriate (or to prove a point).

One look at the Atlanta Hawks' contract collection shows they're hard-wired to take a big midseason swing, and a primary creator remains their most pressing need. Even as they ran roughshod over the league to close last year, their half-court offense was good-not-great material .

Kingston Flemings may eventually be the answer. He probably won't solve all of their problems right now.

Kyrie Irving comes with a pricey salary, but the contract is short term. The Hawks can use his player option next summer to renegotiate a longer deal at a lower number. More importantly, he could lose a step or two and remain an offensive force. The shooting isn't going anywhere, and he can play off other ball-dominant talent—including Flemings.

Jamal Murray straddles a similar line. He doesn't have Kyrie's handle or raw creation, but he's a better defender and can play off anyone. Though the three years and $161.4 million left on his contract are steep, bargain-bin deals for Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu give the Hawks this season and next before it becomes a real problem. Atlanta should cross its fingers for a Denver implosion.

Day'Ron Sharpe rounds out the board as a heftier frontline alternative to Johnson, Okongwu, Jock Landale and a healthy Mo Gueye. While not a shutdown rim protector, he brings good-enough rebounding, physicality and defensive mobility at a backup's price point.

The Boston Celtics feel like they'll wait until the offseason if they go buck wild on the trade market, but Trey Murphy III is Mazzullaball nirvana. His three-point shooting scales to higher volume and movement, and he's a lob target in his own right.

A team-friendly salary through 2028-29 only heightens his appeal. The Celtics can match his money without including Paul George if they're willing to ship out Mitchell Robinson as part of a (mega) package once he's trade-eligible.

Speaking of team-friendly, Scotty Pippen Jr. provides ball-handling, playmaking and defense on the cheap. He is owed under $5.5 million combined over the next two seasons (2027-28 club option) and would spare Boston from overtaxing George, Derrick White or one of the younger wings with too much on-ball work.

Naji Marshall remains trade-eligible after signing his extension with Dallas, where he's dabbled in oversized-point-guard work. Boston also needed outside-in rim pressure before moving Jaylen Brown. Marshall delivers that in spades, and the Celtics have enough floor-spacers to offset his shaky shooting outside floater range.

Now isn't the time for the Brooklyn Nets to go all-in. Their lack of involvement in the Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jaylen Brown sweepstakes is proof they know as much.

Franz Wagner is a worthwhile exception, in large part because he's only all-in from a financial perspective. The Orlando Magic would be moving him under cap-sheet duress after seeing their season go off the rails. Brooklyn has the financial leeway to build around a pricey power wing who's a net additive at both ends. His brother, Mo Wagner, is also Brooklyn's backup center. Just saying.

Younger fliers should otherwise be the Nets' trade-market currency. Ron Holland II typifies the approach with "the dials all go to 11" energy and toughness. Unless he turns into a deadeye shooter, his future with the Detroit Pistons is conveniently up in the air after they doubled-down on the trio of Cade Cunningham, Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson.

Yang Hansen has not shown enough of what makes him special at the NBA level: passing, range and physicality. But he's two impressive summer leagues deep and on a Portland Trail Blazers squad with no fewer than two centers in front of him. Brooklyn has plenty of room to plumb the depths of his game even after bringing back Day'Ron Sharpe.

Mileage will vary on how aggressive the Charlotte Hornets should be pursuing upgrades. They need to see what everyone coalesces into post-LaMelo Ball.

Isaiah Stewart is a happy medium. The Hornets need more rim protection in the middle than the big-man cohort of Naz Reid, Moussa Diabaté, Hannes Steinbach and Ryan Kalkbrenner will provide. Stewart shouldn't cost the moon to extract from Memphis, and he's owed a flat $15 million per year through 2027-28.

In the event Charlotte is willing to swing bigger, Jarrett Allen encapsulates everything it needs. The in-house playmaking ranks will have to prove their mettle to maximize his offensive utility, but he's more of an independent decision-maker than credited.

Onyeka Okongwu has improved as a shooter, passer, rebounder—the whole nine. Prioritizing someone with a little more heft is fine, but his versatility lets him pair nicely with every other big on the roster as part of larger lineups.

Like Allen, Okongwu's availability is predicated on their own teams underachieving. While the Hornets have create-your-own-market assets, they should be rooting for Atlanta and Cleveland implosions and pivots.

The Chicago Bulls are clearly rebuilding. That is surreal to write with a straight face, and it puts them squarely in young-flier and distressed-asset modes.

A long-term big man prospect should be the top focus. Under no circumstances should the Bulls jettison unprotected or lightly protected first-round picks, which might rule out everyone on this list. It still never hurts to ask.

Kel'el Ware has the highest ceiling of the trio. He might be able to space the floor. He might be able to hold his own defensively at the 4 or the 5. He definitely gives Chicago an an explosive, athletic frontcourt with Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson.

Are the Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies worried enough about the long-term health of Dereck Lively II and Zach Edey, respectively, that they're willing to sell low to medium? I'm asking for all of Chicago.

Odds and ends are all that can populate the Cleveland Cavaliers' wish list unless they're moving a core player.

They are hard-capped at the first apron, from which they sit just $45,000 . Their largest matching salary outside the starting five is the sub-$10 million Sam Merrill. After him, it's Jaylon Tyson…who's on the books for under $3.7 million.

Justin Champagnie, Jabari Walker and GG Jackson II are each cheap enough for the Cavs to dream about. All of them can log minutes as a backup 4. Champagnie can sponge up reps as the 2 or 3 as well. Walker can slide up to the 5 in a pinch.

Depth-chart politics are Cleveland's best friend for each of these guys. Champagnie and Jackson are ensconced in crowded wing rotations, and Walker's usage by Philadelphia could plunge if its frontline is ever kinda-sorta healthy.

Kyrie Irving is a fleeting answer to the Dallas Mavericks' lead-guard question even if they don't trade him. They should be dedicated to pursuing anyone who can feasibly change that.

Scoot Henderson immediately springs to mind. He has become a somewhat-trustworthy shooter and doesn't need to dominate the ball. His athletic profile isn't what it was supposed to be, but he can still get into the paint and has a defensive pulse.

Guards galore in Portland plus Henderson's impending restricted free agency could leave him on the chopping block. The opportunity cost of prying him away shouldn't be too stark—particularly if the Blazers have interest in any of Dallas' vets (Max Christie, anyone?).

Reed Sheppard shouldn't technically be available. The best version of him does everything the Houston Rockets' offense needs—most notably drill outside shots of all types. But Sheppard gets targeted on defense and doesn't play with a lot of offensive oomph. Both flaws are liable to trap him in Ime Udoka's doghouse now that Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart are both in town.

Tre Jones isn't a good enough shooter to top this list, but he's the most proven option. A maestro of the mid-range, he adds genuine ball control and standout vision in traffic. Getting him would immediately make life easier on Cooper Flagg and improve the shot quality of any Mavericks center. Dallas is also big enough elsewhere to test out Jones-Kyrie backcourt lineups.

Ball-handling that holds up to playoff pressure should be exactly what the Denver Nuggets are Jones-ing for. Tyus Jones was pretty OK in the postseason last year and DeMar DeRozan is a portrait of stability, but the former is tiny and neither brings much athleticism to the table.

Scoot Henderson would be a nifty flier if the Nuggets can make the math work. He's on the books for $13.6 million, and they're more than $3 million into the second apron. This scenario begs for a third team if Denver, as expected, is looking to cut money.

Gaming out a package is worth the hassle. Henderson shot over 38 percent on spot-up threes last year and immediately becomes one of the Nuggets' best athletes. His defense has improved enough to operate alongside Jamal Murray.

Kris Dunn admittedly won't bring much ball-handling. But he's a willing screener who defends with All-NBA hellfire for extended pockets. A Zeke Nnaji-plus-enough-sweeteners package could get the Nuggets out of the second apron if one of those sweeteners is a dispensable young player.

Jordan Goodwin belongs on this list if Denver thinks it'll get enough supplemental ball-handling from Christian Braun and Cam Johnson this year. His three-year, $19 million contract is a pittance, and at 6'3", he spends equitable time defending wings and guards. Like Dunn, nobody's writing love songs about his jumper. But he's at 37.3 percent from three over the past two seasons, and the Nuggets need defensive firepower more than offensive polish.

Gauging the Detroit Pistons' ambitions is difficult for the time being. Poking around Austin Reaves ahead of free agency suggests they're itching for a splash, but their actions imply they want to see whether more spacing plus improvement from Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren can fill the No. 2 scorer/creator void.

Detroit should abandon all pretense if it means getting Deni Avdija. He can drive the offense or play off Cade Cunningham while checking the "big-picture 4" box. He is the player you put pretty much everything on the table to land—particularly when his salary is small enough you wouldn't need to include Thompson (who's poison-pilled post-extension anyway).

Portland would be bananas to ship out Avdija now. But he's too cheap to extend, and the Ja Morant trade makes it harder to renegotiate-and-extend him next summer. Who knows whether team governor Tom Dundon is willing to back up the Brink's truck for his prize forward if and when he can. The private-equity thing to do is sell him at the peak of his value.

We continue playing the greatest hits after Avdija. Michael Porter Jr. and Tyler Herro both supercharge the spacing and offensive optionality. In Herro's case, Detroit's ball-handling and table-setting would improve.

The Pistons won't get either of them for nothing, but as soon-to-be free agents, they're less likely to require a king's ransom. The same holds true for their next contracts. Detroit shouldn't have a huge issue affording either one of them past this season.

Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Moses Moody won't be ready to rock until god knows when. It took one open practice for Stephen Curry to scare the hell out of everyone by tweaking his ankle. Head coach Steve Kerr is already apologizing to fans .

This Golden State Warriors season is cooked.

Rather than pretend they should be skulking around mid-tier markets, this is a wishlist of epic proportions. The Dubs shouldn't do anything unless it has the chance to give them everything.

Maybe the Denver Nuggets' season veers so far into the abyss that both the franchise and its superstar lifer reconsider his extension promise . Perhaps Aday Mara is so good so fast that the Oklahoma City Thunder end up rethinking their monster commitment to Chet Holmgren amid an expected belly flop into second-apron territory next season . Maybe the Cleveland Cavaliers self-destruct after going all-in multiple times over and seek to restock their draft-pick cupboard the only way they now can: by moving Evan Mobley.

None of this is likely. That's the point. The Warriors are so far away from a championship-contender formula, waiting out unlikely trade opportunities is the only sensible way forward.

Offense remains the Houston Rockets' biggest question mark. This big board attacks it from different angles and to varying ambition.

Trey Murphy III should be on the Rockets' radar even if Fred VanVleet looks great post-ACL injury and Reed Sheppard goes kaboom in Year 3. The 26-year-old soups up half-court spacing without dominating the ball and has enough size to slot into the 2, 3 or 4.

Ryan Rollins could feasibly claim the No. 1 spot on this list if VanVleet doesn't look like himself or Sheppard's play drives Ime Udoka to distraction. His shot selection can be spotty and he's not the cleanest ball-handler, but playing for the Rockets could give him a more structured role than he had with the Bucks. A higher-stakes environment might help him address those weaknesses.

Rollins doesn't get picked on as frequently at the defensive end as Sheppard and has shown more panache on his drives. Houston would have to contend with his free agency next summer ($4 million player option), but he should run cheaper than VanVleet is now.

The Rockets won't need much big-man insurance if Steven Adams stays healthy and they roll out more Jabari Smith Jr.-at-the-5 arrangements. We're talking about fairly large ifs in both cases. Jalen Smith's floor-spacing and rebounding are better safety nets than present-day Clint Capela. And at a $9.4 million price point, Houston should be able to game out his arrival without entering the tax.

Backup bigs and wings loom as the Indiana Pacers' biggest needs until (or unless) they prove otherwise. The former takes precedence, because Ivica Zubac can't play 48 minutes per game and Jay Huff is coming off a down year from beyond the arc.

Yves Missi is wildly imperfect at the offensive end but could suddenly develop quality hands and touch around the basket thanks to the magic of playing alongside Tyrese Haliburton. The idea of acquiring a center on his rookie-scale deal will appeal to a franchise nearly $6 million into the luxury tax and juggling an expensive core in the years ahead.

Here's a list of every player averaging at least 10 defensive rebounds and three made triples per 100 possessions since 2022: Luka Dončić, Jayson Tatum, Kevin Love, Victor Wembanyama and Jaylin Williams. 'Nuff said.

Well, not quite. J-Will would top the board if not for his $7.8 million salary. That's far from exorbitant, but incorporating him gets complicated if the Pacers are trying to shed $6 million in salary. It's more likely Aday Mara prompts Oklahoma City to trade J-Will than Indiana pays the tax.

Jordan Walsh can defend all over the floor and only makes $2.4 million this season. His extension was cheap enough at three years and $15 million that the poison pill provision isn't a huge hurdle. His importance to the Celtics is the bigger obstacle. He started games in the preseason. Indy will have a harder time calling about him if he stays inside the opening five.

Collecting first-rounders is standard rebuilding-team procedure. It's even more essential for a Los Angeles Clippers franchise that was just stripped of five future picks.

Jrue Holiday goes against the bigger-picture emphasis at first glance. Hear me out, though: He's a high-character vet who still provides ball-handling, some scoring and plenty of defense. Putting him in a lineup with Keaton Wagler and Darius Garland actually makes a ton of sense.

The Portland Trail Blazers just so happen to be teeming with guard-types and will need to clear off money that's on the books past this season if they want to renegotiate-and-extend Deni Avdija. L.A. has the expiring contracts to make a deal work.

Nikola Topić represents the opposite end of the rebuilding-team spectrum: a second-draft guy. Health issues, including a cancer diagnosis , and an absurdly deep Oklahoma City Thunder roster have pretty much zeroed out his opportunities.

L.A. is an ideal landing spot with the Clippers in nothing-to-lose territory. There is some redundancy with the team's other ball-handlers, but Garland and Wagler can play off anyone. The Clippers can worry about pecking-order problems if Topić turns into something.

Combo forwards and backup bigs should be all the rage for Los Angeles Lakers trade-machine enthusiasts. The problem? They have just one first-round swap and three future second-rounders to dangle alongside matching salary. Including rookie Cameron Carr glitzes up any package, but he should be considered off limits unless the Lakers are landing a member of their closing unit.

PJ Washington comes close to meeting that criterion. He fits like a glove next to Walker Kessler at the 5 when his three-ball is falling, and though he's not a defender who turns the water off, he can be moved up and down the matchup ladder. Head coach JJ Redick can even use him for backup-center tick when Kessler is catching a breather.

Assuming Carr won't be on the table, Los Angeles' best chance of landing Washington is more about the Dallas Mavericks. The Lakers need him to tumble down a crowded frontcourt hierarchy.

Derrick Jones Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe are more realistic for what L.A. can offer. Going on 30 this February, Jones remains athletic enough to check tough defensive assignments and get up and down the floor. He tends to hit juuust enough of his wide-open threes to remain in a playoff rotation.

Sharpe would be a huge defensive upgrade at the backup-5 spot to Sandro Mamukelashvili and the ghost of Kevon Looney. Thanks to Mamu's shooting and driving, the Lakers could play both bigs together rather easily in bench mobs. Most critically, Sharpe is top-end insurance against Kessler missing any time.

Ty Jerome, Scotty Pippen Jr., Cam Spencer and Jaylen Wells are all quality backcourt players. The Memphis Grizzlies need someone at the 1 or the 2 with the potential to really pop.

Not that they should be in a rush to make a big swing. That's why Shaedon Sharpe is at the top. He's going to miss much of this season with a meniscus tear in his right knee. The Grizzlies have the timeline to take it slow with him.

For all his defensive flaws, Sharpe offers bonkers shot-making possibilities. His off-ball movement has always stood out, although Memphis will want a higher-end floor general if it's going to nuke some of his more damning impulses. If the Portland Trail Blazers are looking to offload long-term salary to make way for a Deni Avdija renegotiate-and-extend next summer, Memphis is a logical trade partner.

Injuries make Darius Garland seem older than he is in reality. At 26, he is decidedly timeline-proof. He can shimmy between running the offense on-ball and working away from it. The chemistry between him and Cam Boozer could be heavenly.

You're either smitten with Reed Sheppard's shooting and defensive playmaking or turned off by his slight frame and lack of on-ball gusto going downhill. Either way, boom-or-bust, he's a higher-end backcourt prospect than anyone the Grizzlies have now. The Houston Rockets should be on Memphis' speed dial if it looks like Sheppard is the eighth man in their rotation.

The Miami Heat have adequately stocked their supporting cast with shooting if Klay Thompson ever moves out of Brickscayne Bay. But they remain hard-up for ball-handling that doesn't shrink the floor.

Cam Spencer would take care of that—and then some. He averaged 5.6 assists while swishing 44.9 percent of his 4.6 three-point attempts for the Memphis Grizzlies last season and plays enough defense that he could close games. Bake in a contract that has him under team control through 2028-29 for less than $3 million per year, and the Heat shouldn't be above sending out a first-round swap or even a conditional 2029 first.

Daniss Jenkins' shooting hasn't extended to off-the-dribble opportunities, but he drilled 47.7 percent of his spot-up triples last year and is a serviceable offensive steward. The Detroit Pistons' motivation for trading him would be to open up run for Ebuka Okorie and get out in front of Jenkins' foray into 2027 restricted free agency.

Despite setting the world on fire for 15 games last season, Ty Jerome could be the more gettable Memphis guard. He isn't a billboard for health and has more defensive limitations than Spencer. His shot-making, handle and passing are also enough to (probably) start and close for the Heat.

If it looks like Miami is avoiding the lottery, would Memphis accept a 2028 swap and 2029 first attached to Nikola Jović for Spencer or Jerome (and other money)? Failing that, the Heat have the more reasonable contracts of Davion Mitchell and Bobby Portis Jr. to use as salary anchors.

Cleveland's 2031 first-round pick (via Denver)

The Denver Nuggets are inside the second apron. The Milwaukee Bucks have over $12.5 million in tax room and a $25.5 million traded player exception burning a hole in their pocket.

Let's make a cost-cutting deal that reroutes Cleveland's 2031 first-rounder to Wisconsin.

Apart from targeting more future first-rounders, the Bucks have so many guys that they should consider taking on distressed big-name assets, just to see what happens. This approach also jibes with them not controlling their own first-rounder again until 2030.

Can they get a Zion Williamson peek without having to give up a first-rounder? Or help the Orlando Magic shave future salary while giving up modest value for Paolo Banchero, a flawed 23-year-old who nevertheless fits the timeline and has an All-Star appearance and smattering of playoff moments under his belt? The Bucks should totally find out.

Adding size off the bench would go a long way for the Minnesota Timberwolves. Their primary backup 4-5 options are a mixture of Joan Beringer, Trey Lyles and Cody Williams. Sliding Jaden McDaniels up to the 4 in certain instances will help, but the Wolves could run into overarching issues if Beringer, Rudy Gobert or Jonathan Kuminga find themselves in foul trouble (or out).

Rasheer Fleming would be a dynamite fit. He is long, can defend a bunch of positions, has potential to gobble up small-ball 5 minutes and likes to crash the offensive glass. His contract is a bargain. He's under team control at a combined $7.4 million. Though he seemed in line for a bigger role with Phoenix this season, the Miles Bridges acquisition changes the calculus.

Jabari Walker gets to the rim, rebounds and can also be moved around the positional spectrum on defense. His importance to Philadelphia has skyrocketed amid frontcourt injuries, but he stands to get lost in the shuffle if and when Dominick Barlow, Adem Bona, Dean Wade, LeBron James and Joel Embiid are healthy at the same time.

Micah Potter hit some ridiculous threes as a member of the Indiana Pacers last season and grabs a few more rebounds than you'd think. Portland has a trillion centers, and he could plausibly drop behind Donovan Clingan, Robert Williams III and Yang Hansen in the pecking order. Minnesota should be crossing its fingers that he does.

The New Orleans Pelicans are running their operation like they have a prayer of being good this season. Everyone in this universe and 99.9 percent of all alternate ones disagree. New Orleans shouldn't be aggressive buyers as a result.

At the same time, if they're going to give the roster a fighting chance, they should transact like they mean it. In other words, trade for a frontcourt player who fits with Derik Queen or Zion Williamson—or both.

Myles Turner better have a second home in The Big Easy with how often he's tied to the Pelicans. He's less appealing as a player now, but more attractive to acquire. New Orleans won't have to give up the haul it once needed to land him. Building something around Jordan Poole's expiring contract might get 'er done.

Jaylin Williams' defensive rebounding and willingness to fire away from deep are a nice complement to both Zion and Queen. His $7.8 million salary in each of the next two seasons is a nicer complement to the Pelicans' books.

Aaron Gordon is the most aggressive name here. He does almost everything the Pelicans' frontcourt would need alongside Queen or Zion: defend, space, move without the ball, etc. The rebounding might be touch-and-go, but hey, that's an issue in New Orleans now.

Gordon's path to the chopping block is the toughest to peg. The Pelicans need the Denver Nuggets to stumble relative to other superpowers and enter roster-reorientation mode beyond shopping Cam Johnson and Christian Braun.

Andre Drummond and James Wiseman are worthwhile regular-season heirs apparent to Mitchell Robinson and Ariel Hukporti, respectively. Whether the New York Knicks have enough depth behind Karl-Anthony Towns to feel good about every playoff matchup is a separate matter.

Moussa Diabaté and Dylan Cardwell check the offensive rebounding and defensive mobility boxes. Diabaté is in his contract year and could wind up being a rental, but Cardwell is under team control through 2028-29 for a combined $7.4 million. Both can log minutes alongside Towns—an option New York doesn't have with Drummond or Wiseman.

Luka Garza falling behind Robinson and Neemias Queta in the Boston Celtics' big-man hierarchy is the Knicks' opening to get him out of Beantown. Ditto for his impending free agency next summer. After drilling over 43 percent of his threes last year, he is another tall body who can play beside Towns if New York so chooses.

Garza doesn't have the defensive malleability of Diabate or Cardwell, but he's a stealthy presence on the second-chance glass. Through five NBA seasons, he has notched a career offensive rebounding percentage of 15.8. That mark ranks eighth in the entire league among everyone who has logged at least 2,000 total minutes.

Forwards standing 6'7" or taller are on the Oklahoma City Thunder's mind. At least, that is what their offseason offer sheet to Spencer Jones suggests.

Going after Rasheer Fleming is an extension of that approach. The jury remains out on his three-point shooting, but at 6'9" and with a wingspan over 7'5" , he's a defensive worker bee who can even tackle select big-man assignments. His willingness to crash the offensive glass is a plus, and a contract that pays him $7.4 million total through 2028-29 is just what Oklahoma City's jam-packed books ordered.

Derrick Jones Jr. still has the athletic profile to fit the Thunder's style. The shooting is forever dicey, but he's drilled more than 35 percent of his threes over the past two regular seasons. His $10.5 million salary is easy enough for Oklahoma City to acquire and comes off the books after this year.

Josh Minott follows the Rasheer Fleming blueprint. He isn't as long, but he can rumble with a bunch of different positions on defense. If he's anywhere near the 40 percent clip he shot from three last season, the Thunder should be smitten with both his fit and the two-year, $9 million contract he just started.

Newly minted head coach Sean Sweeney can change the Orlando Magic's offense. He can't change the personnel. The Magic haven't ranked in the top half of both three-point volume and efficiency since 2011-12. Anyone who nudges them further in that direction should pique their curiosity.

Naz Reid tops the list if Orlando is willing to do something spicy. Its books are within striking distance of the second apron , but a package of Anthony Black and Wendell Carter Jr. cuts both short- and long-term payroll when factoring in Black's next contract.

Svi Mikhailiuk is 6'7" and just banged in 40.8 percent of his 7.5 three-point attempts per 36 minutes last season. Between that and his $3.9 million salary, the Magic should be all over him.

Deuce McBride is in a contract year, which theoretically complicates Orlando's situation. But he's a better shooter than Black who, because of his size, will cost way less to retain. Acquiring McBride would be an excellent hedge against AB pricing himself out of town or the front office electing to move him ahead of the Feb. 11 trade deadline.

Close your eyes and point at a Philadelphia 76ers frontcourt player. Chances are pretty high they're an injury risk…if not already injured.

Chasing after backup bigs is Philly's default as a result.

Moussa Diabaté's offensive rebounding and two-way mobility are an upgrade over any true center the Sixers currently have behind Joel Embiid. His entry into 2027 free agency is a potential deterrent, but it's also what makes him gettable. For a team right up against the first apron that doesn't have much dispensable salary, his $2.5 million contract is a spreadsheet thirst trap.

Luka Garza won't always be the answer over someone like (a healthy) Adem Bona. But his floor-spacing adds an intriguing element to the rotation. Philly can get away with playing him alongside another big if it's looking to upsize. Even with free agency on the horizon, his $2.8 million salary is a capologist's fever dream.

Familiarize yourself with Karlo Matković if you haven't already. He would thrive in the Sixers' uptempo attack after live rebounds, shot 42.2 percent on 90 three-point attempts last year and has a combination of sneaky athleticism and good hands that render him an operable lob threat. His $2.3 million salary is both teensy and expiring, and he's not someone who will have many suitors during free agency if things work out in Philly.

Imagine a world in which Devin Booker doesn't need to be the Phoenix Suns' top scorer and setup man. What a concept!

Darius Garland's scattershot health bill shouldn't scare the Suns. They have just one tradeable first-round pick. They don't have the assets to be choosy. Garland's shooting, fidgety cadence in the lane and broader passing vision would make life easier for Booker and crank up the play-finishing utility of Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach. Attaching Jalen Green's contract to another just about gets the salary-matching job done.

Dejounte Murray has looked fairly steady coming off an Achilles injury that limited him to 14 appearances last year. He isn't a first-rate playmaker, but he's still a higher-end initiator than Collin Gillespie.

Although Terrence Shannon Jr.'s playmaking is often conflated with getting downhill at top speed, he has flashed live-dribble poise coming around ball screens and throws pretty good lobs. Maluach would eat . That alone should get Phoenix picking up the phone.

Fortunately for the Suns, Shannon had the Minnesota Timberwolves waxing about the importance of putting the ball in his hands following last year's playoffs. Good luck figuring out that possession math with LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards, Ayo Dosunmu, Jonathan Kuminga and Jaden McDaniels on the roster. Phoenix should use the breadth of players blocking him to its advantage.

Speaking with yours truly on Hardwood Knocks , Locked On Blazers ' Mike Richman identified another point-of-attack defender as the Portland Trail Blazers' biggest need. My first instinct was additional shooting, but Damian Lillard and Ja Morant have to be protected on the less-glamorous end. The current roster puts a lot of stress on Toumani Camara while asking Scoot Henderson and the aging Jrue Holiday to guard above their heads.

Nickeil Alexander-Walker is the "Why choose between shooting and defense?" option. The reigning Most Improved Player is disruptive both on and off the ball and downing 39 percent of his treys over the past four seasons.

Convincing the Atlanta Hawks to move him will take a Godfather offer. The Blazers have assets to throw around, and NAW's mid-level contract is attractive enough to toss them at him.

Jalen Suggs' shooting comes and goes, but he's a defensive dynamo and probably an underrated passer. Payroll concerns are coming for the Orlando Magic— and they know it. Packages built around some combination of Shaedon Sharpe, Scoot Henderson, Robert Williams and draft equity might get them thinking. Doubly so if they want to keep soon-to-be-restricted-agent Anthony Black past this season.

Jaylen Wells is making minimum-contract money this season and next and routinely covers the other team's best offensive players. That combination is enough to overlook the shaky shooting. The Memphis Grizzlies shouldn't be dying to move him, but he's not far away from requiring a new deal (2027-28 team option) and they're in the early stages of a rebuild.

Assuming the Sacramento Kings aren't prepared to short-circuit their future for the instant gratification of chasing the 10-seed, they are in full-on second-draft mode.

Bilal Coulibaly is in a contract year and at risk of getting buried by Washington's wing surplus. His offensive wheelhouse remains TBD, but he's a pesky defender across up to four positions.

Jarace Walker is threatening to graduate from the "second-draft guy" discussion. But the Indiana Pacers are in the tax, which they never pay, and he's in a contract year himself. Both tidbits should be music to the Kings' ears.

Tidjane Salaün has the physical tools to be...anything. A little over two years into his career, this has resulted in a quasi-formless archetype. He did, however, make strides last year as a shooter and rebounder and should be a transition lightning rod.

Unless the Charlotte Hornets believe he's their long-term answer at the 4, they have enough combo bigs for the Kings to inquire about a Salaün flier.

Anything the San Antonio Spurs consider should be viewed through the lens of cherry-topping their best lineup. If Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox are all in it, the final spot should be rounded out with a combo forward.

Trey Murphy III would be divine. He isn't as imposing as Tobias Harris, but the Spurs are test-running Devin Vassell alongside the three guards. Murphy is an upgrade as an off-ball player and offers more size.

Cam Johnson falls into a similar bucket. Murphy has him beat as an athlete (and contract), but Johnson is the more dynamic passer. His foray into 2027 free agency must be a factor, but the Denver Nuggets' financial situation should also make him easier to acquire.

Tari Eason is the biggest swing of all. The five-year, $81.5 million contract he just signed fits San Antonio's short- and long-term salary structure, and he remains a defensive menace. If the Spurs could guarantee he'd down more than 34 to 36 percent of his threes, or that Houston would be open to a shakeup, he'd be the best option on the board.

Shooting and passing top the Toronto Raptors' list of needs. Kyrie Irving takes care of both while creating a filthy offensive trio with Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard.

Aging up the roster even further would be a risk, and Kyrie's $39.5 million isn't cheap. But the Raptors have two other stars to streamline his workload, and they can use his player option next summer as a chance to negotiate a longer deal with a smaller annual number.

Jalen Suggs doesn't receive enough credit for passing. The shooting can be rough, but he hit 39.3 percent of his spot-up threes last year. He also upgrades the top of Toronto's defense. Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett are overstretched in prominent on-ball roles.

The Raptors should put a pin in Karl-Anthony Towns' extension standoff with the New York Knicks while they're at it. He isn't always the defender we witnessed during last year's playoffs, but the spacing, driving, passing and rebounding diminish the need for Toronto's offensive upgrade to come in the backcourt.

And yes, the huge salaries here are by design. The Raptors' books are better built for a bigger move. They don't have the second-rung contracts to swing middle.

Isaiah Hartenstein (trade-eligible Dec. 15)

Signing-and-trading Walker Kessler to the Los Angeles Lakers left a hole in the Utah Jazz's center rotation. It has grown even larger following Jusuf Nurkić's right toe injury. Luckily for the Jazz, they have the assets to go big-name hunting.

Isaiah Hartenstein would be an ideal get. He promises physicality, rebounding, passing and a trusty ol' flip shot. Utah can play him alongside Jaren Jackson Jr. without issue and doesn't need to worry about him griping if head coach Will Hardy deems it necessary to run out JJJ-at-the-5 to close games.

To that end, all Jazz fans should be rooting for Aday Mara to dominate from the jump. That's the pathway to the Oklahoma City Thunder getting out in front of next year's second-apron crunch by dealing Hartenstein.

Get ready to hear Jarrett Allen's name mentioned a ton in Utah circles this year. He isn't the most imposing big, but he would boost the Jazz's rim protection and rebounding and does a ton of ancillary things on offense beyond finishing. He (probably) costs more than anyone on this list to land, so that's food for thought.

Onyeka Okongwu isn't a towering big himself. But the shooting, passing, rebounding and switchability are perfect for this Jazz roster. A frontcourt built around him and Jackson may not board every miss, but it'd be among the three or four most versatile defensive tandems around.

Wing shooting that doesn't come at the expense of defense profiles as the Washington Wizards' biggest pain point. Aaron Nesmith's scrappiness, movement and outside touch fit like a glove alongside this team's cast of on-ball-leaning talent.

Prying him away from the Indiana Pacers is an "over my dead body" undertaking. They aren't exactly teeming with two-way wings themselves. The Wizards have enough assets to get the conversation started, particularly if Indiana stumbles off its championship-contender arc.

Cam Johnson could become collateral damage of the Denver Nuggets inevitably getting out of the second apron. Washington should be among the first in line for his passing, shooting and overall feel if that's the case. He's not anchoring a perimeter defense on his own, but he's also not capsizing it.

Max Strus is an excellent stab-in-the-dark option should the Wizards want to play it safe. His $16.7 million salary comes off the books after this season, and it shouldn't cost too much to land him when he's starting the year injured . If the price is right, his shooting and playmaking are worth the wait.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: LeBron James' Usage as Center Explained by Joel Embiid After 76ers' Win in NBA Opener vs. Knicks
articles.summary: With a lack of size behind Joel Embiid on the Philadelphia 76ers' depth chart, head coach Nick Nurse gave LeBron James some run at center during Tuesday's 106-100 season-opening victory over the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
With a lack of size behind Joel Embiid on the Philadelphia 76ers' depth chart, head coach Nick Nurse gave LeBron James some run at center during Tuesday's 106-100 season-opening victory over the New York Knicks.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Embiid explained he was the one who suggested James play at the five spot due in part to how the officials were calling the game:

"I suggested that to the guys, the coaching staff, because I just felt like the way they were calling fouls, I just felt like — and I was just being honest — I wasn't going to be as aggressive as I should be on defense, having three fouls, wanting to stay on the floor. I just told them I thought we should do that."

Embiid received his third foul late in the second quarter with the 76ers trailing 50-46. Nurse subbed him out to bring in Anfernee Simons in a small-ball lineup in an attempt to spur some offensive production, but putting them at risk on defense with James primarily matched up against Karl-Anthony Towns.

Nurse also addressed the move by noting it helped guard against the Knicks' pick-and-roll usage.

"[We discussed putting] a 4-man on KAT, because there's so many pick-and-rolls with him and [Jalen] Brunson that gives you some versatility to play some other coverages," Nurse said. "I think it was good. ... Over the long haul, it was very good for us, I think."

The 76ers were able to stay close during that stretch with the Knicks holding a 58-54 advantage going into halftime. Philadelphia came out on fire in the second half by outscoring New York 29-18 in the third quarter, with James, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown putting up 20 of those 29 points.

James finished with 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in his first game with the 76ers.

Neither team shot the ball particularly well, but the Sixers made enough plays on both ends to steal a win from the defending champs on ring night at Madison Square Garden.

Next up for the 76ers is a matchup against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday in the home opener at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

articles.title: LeBron James' Trash Talk With Knicks Fan Shown in Viral Videos From 76ers' Win in NBA Opener
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James had words with a fan Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden during the Sixers' season-opening, 106-100 win over the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James had words with a fan Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden during the Sixers' season-opening, 106-100 win over the New York Knicks.

James appeared to respond to a fan calling him "soft," as he countered by saying, "Ain't nothing soft in the midwest. I don't know what the f--k you talking about. I'm not from the west coast, I'm from Ohio, baby. ... F--k is you talking about?"

At one point, acclaimed director and longtime Knicks fan Spike Lee stood up from his usual courtside seat and seemingly tried to communicate something to LeBron:

Per Dan Gelston of the Associated Press, Lee was "trying to play peacemaker" in that moment.

Gelston also mentioned the Knicks fans' chants of, "We don't want you," directed toward James after James recently admitted that he may have signed with New York had the franchise not won the NBA championship last season.

It was a celebratory night at MSG with the Knicks raising their first championship banner since 1973, but LeBron and the Sixers did indeed play spoiler.

The 41-year-old James did a little bit of everything in his first regular-season game as a member of the 76ers, recording 14 points on 5-of-13 shooting to go along with nine rebounds and seven assists.

LeBron had plenty of help as well with Tyrese Maxey scoring a game-high 28 points, Jaylen Brown adding 19 points and Joel Embiid registering 13 points and 11 rebounds.

It won't be long before Philly and New York meet again, as the Sixers are scheduled to host the Knicks next week on Oct. 30.

articles.title: De'Aaron Fox Shades Chet Holmgren After Flagrant Foul, On-Court Fight in Spurs' Loss to Thunder
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs wasted little time reigniting their intense rivalry when De'Aaron Fox received a Flagrant 1 foul for a play against Chet Holmgren in the second quarter.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs wasted little time reigniting their intense rivalry when De'Aaron Fox received a Flagrant 1 foul for a play against Chet Holmgren in the second quarter.

Fox had his arm wrapped around Holmgren's waist, then the Thunder center fell to the ground trying to catch a pass, leading to a skirmish on the court between the two teams.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Fox implied Holmgren was doing some good acting with how he sold the fall.

"[If] somebody grabs you like that and you go flying on the floor like that, you've got other problems to worry about," Fox said. "I didn't throw him that hard, I promise you."

The aftermath of the initial play also cost the Thunder because Jalen Williams, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams all received a technical foul. Holmgren made both of his flagrant free throws. Victor Wembanyama made both technical free throws.

So the end result was negated with both teams getting two points out of the situation.

Holmgren's involvement in the play does add more spice given the well-documented rivalry between him and Wembanyama that dates back to 2021 when Holmgren led Team USA to a victory over Wembanyama and France in the FIBA U-19 World Cup gold-medal game.

One of the big storylines coming out of the Western Conference Finals last season was Holmgren's struggles against the Spurs, particularly his four points on two field-goal attempts in Oklahoma City's Game 7 loss.

Tuesday night provided a modicum of redemption, as Holmgren finished with 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks to help the Thunder start the 2026-27 season with a 116-104 win over the Spurs.

articles.title: LeBron James' Box Score From 76ers' Opener, How It Compares to NBA Debuts With Cavs, Heat, Lakers
articles.summary: Playing for the fourth different team of his illustrious NBA career, LeBron James helped the Philadelphia 76ers go on the road and knock off the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Playing for the fourth different team of his illustrious NBA career, LeBron James helped the Philadelphia 76ers go on the road and knock off the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks on Tuesday night.

Although LeBron contributed to the Sixers' 106-100 victory, his statistical production was somewhat modest when compared to his debut performances with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and Los Angeles Lakers:

James managed just 14 points on 5-of-13 shooting, but he filled up the stat sheet with nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and only one turnover.

Most importantly, LeBron had a ton of help from his teammates, as Tyrese Maxey scored a game-high 28 points, Jaylen Brown scored 19, Joel Embiid had 13 points and 11 rebounds, and both Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope scored in double figures off the bench.

articles.title: LeBron James has heated exchange with Knicks fan as MSG crowd reminds him: 'We don't want you!'
articles.summary: James said last month he had dreams of signing in New York and helping the Knicks end their NBA title drought before he joined the Sixers.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers spoiled the New York Knicks' NBA title banner-raising party Tuesday night, but the fans inside Madison Square Garden made sure to give one of the city's newest residents a rude reception.

LeBron James was not given a warm greeting by the New Yorkers in attendance, with the crowd at one point chanting, "We don't want you!" as he was at the free-throw line early in the game.

Near the end of the first half, James had a back-and-forth with fans sitting courtside while the Knicks were at the foul line. The conversation, as relayed by NBC's Mike Tirico, was about James and his use of a helicopter to travel between Philadelphia and New York City, where he now resides.

At one point during the interactions, Spike Lee, dressed in his best Knicks suit for the occasion, attempted to play peacemaker.

"Hey, LeBron, just because you have a helicopter and you live in New York doesn't mean we're gonna cheer for you," the fan said, according to Tirico.

James would continue his back-and-forth with the fans saying, "I'm not from the West Coast. I'm Ohio, baby. […] F*ck you talking about?"

The 41-year-old James would finish with 14 points, 9 rebounds and 7 assists during the Sixers' 106-100 win .

It was well-documented after he signed with the Sixers that James had thoughts about coming to the Knicks during free agency. He told reporters during training camp that he had "visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden" and ending his career with the franchise to help them win an NBA title. But after they defeated the Spurs in June's NBA Finals, James decided against pursuing the move .

After the game, when asked about the Sixers ruining the big night for the Knicks and their fans, James disagreed with the sentiment.

"I wouldn't say that," James said . "It was a great night for New York fans. Fifty-plus years. I was a part of that at one point where we hadn't won a major championship in Cleveland in over 50 years. The fans will never forget this moment."

articles.title: Wemby Talks Struggles vs. Thunder After Ending Up on Wrong Side of NBA History With Rare Stat
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama's 2026-27 NBA season got off to a less-than-ideal start during a 116-104 home loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama's 2026-27 NBA season got off to a less-than-ideal start during a 116-104 home loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday.

Wemby did not make his first field goal until the final seconds of the third quarter. That came after he missed his first 12 shots of the game and the season.

According to Elias (h/t ESPN's Michael C. Wright ), Wembanyama's 12 misses before his first make tied for the second-most consecutive shots missed to start a season-opening game in the play-by-play era, which began in 1997-98.

Bold Predictions for 2026-27 NBA Season 🔮

Wembanyama ended up going just 1-for-13 from the field in the game, although he did finish with 12 points thanks to making 10 of his 12 free-throw attempts. The 7'4" Frenchman also chipped in 13 rebounds, six blocks and three assists.

After Tuesday's uncharacteristic performance, Wemby told reporters what he believes he needs to do in order to play more like himself moving forward.

"I need to go back to playing the basketball I like," Wembanyama said. "This is not the sport I like right here. I've got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. I'm good when I have fun. I missed a lot of shots I usually don't miss. But after that, I didn't go back to these shots, and I wasn't decisive. I might be overthinking it. I don't need to do more. I need to think less probably."

During last season's Western Conference Finals against the Thunder, Wembanyama was dominant, averaging 27.3 points, 10.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 2.7 blocks over the course of the seven-game series.

Thunder center Chet Holmgren had no answers for Wemby at the time, although Holmgren did manage to hold him in check on Tuesday night.

Tuesday marked the first of what could be many meetings between the Spurs and Thunder during the regular season and playoffs this season, so Wembanyama should have plenty of opportunities to bounce back from his disappointing performance in the opener.

articles.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder shut down Victor Wembanyama to roll past Spurs on opening night
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama opened the game by missing his first 12 shots in what was the worst shooting start to any contest in his career.
articles.body: The NBA's reigning two-time MVP is picking up right where he left off. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Oklahoma City Thunder to a 116-104 win over Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night to kick off the 2026-27 NBA season. Gilgeous-Alexander looked as confident as ever coming out of the offseason and dropped 32 points with 5 rebounds and 4 assists. The Thunder pretty easily shut down Wembanyama, too. He had just 12 points and 13 rebounds, and had only a single made field goal on the night. Wembanyama bolted off the court as soon as the final buzzer sounded."We're just happy to be back," Gilgeous-Alexander said on NBC after the win. "The NBA's back. It's a longer summer when you don't win, and we felt that this summer. We're just happy to be back. "[It's] one of 82. This doesn't prove anything, this doesn't mean anything. … We took a step in the right direction."Thunder run away in heated first halfThe rivalry between the Thunder and Spurs heated up almost instantly on Tuesday night. After a contentious stretch early, Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox suddenly grabbed Thunder star Chet Holmgren by the hip and slammed him down as they were jostling for position in the paint. Holmgren, the 7-foot-1 center, is almost a full foot taller than Fox. That, of course, led to a pretty big scuffle in the paint. In the end, Wembanyama, Jalen Williams, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams all received technical fouls for their actions. Fox was hit with a flagrant, too. Flagrant foul 1 on De’Aaron Fox for throwing Chet Holmgren to the ground.Victor Wembanyama, Jaylin Williams, Jalen Williams, and Kenrich Williams all pick up technical fouls after the Spurs and Thunder get into a scuffle in the second quarter of tonight’s season opener.…— Brett Siegel (@BrettSiegelNBA) October 21, 2026 But that sparked a huge run for the Thunder. They broke the game open with a quick 9-0 run after the altercation and ended up pushing it to 22-3 to take a 26-point lead at its peak. Gilgeous-Alexander dropped 16 points in the first half, and the Thunder took a 21-point lead into the break. They had 11 different players score, and went an impressive 10 of 14 from the 3-point line.Wembanyama, meanwhile, struggled offensively. While he had three blocks in the first 24 minutes, he went a rough 0 of 7 from the field. The Spurs opened the second half about as good as they could have and cut the game back to single digits after a 14-3 run. But it didn't last long, thanks in part to a huge sequence from Thunder rookie Aday Mara. The big man stuffed Wembanyama at the rim and then threw down his own lob at the other end just moments later.Aday Mara MAKING PLAYS in his first NBA game 🔥Big-time swat at the rim.Two-hand alley-oop slam.The Thunder lead in Q3! pic.twitter.com/YJpmoBAm8J— NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 Wembanyama finally got his first bucket of the night to fall right at the buzzer of the third quarter on a reverse slam. He had missed his first 12 shots of the night, which is the worst shooting start in any game of his career. But the dunk cut the deficit to 13 points and kept the Spurs within striking distance. In the end, though, the Spurs just couldn't recover from their first-half struggles. The Thunder expertly survived one last push in the fourth to cruise to the 12-point win.Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 24 points and seven rebounds. Dylan Harper added 18 points, and Fox finished with 14 points and seven rebounds.Jared McCain added 20 points off the bench for the Thunder to go with Gilgeous-Alexander's night. McCain made a career-high six 3-pointers, too. Holmgren finished with 14 points and seven rebounds.While it's only the first night of the regular season, and these two teams will meet again plenty of times over the next several months, the Thunder clearly were itching for revenge after last season's loss in the Western Conference finals. This rivalry is, clearly, alive and well.

articles.title: Yahoo Sports launches new fantasy basketball game for NBA on Prime Broadcasts
articles.summary: Designed to complement season-long Yahoo Fantasy formats, Perfect 5 gives fans a fun, easy way to engage around each week's exclusive NBA on Prime coverage.
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports is giving fans yet another way to play fantasy basketball this season with the launch of Perfect 5 , a free-to-play game connected to each week's marquee NBA on Prime matchups. Designed to complement season-long fantasy basketball, the new format features weekly roster building and scoring. Specifically:

Fans pick five players from the games featured in each week's NBA on Prime doubleheader.

Each player has a salary between $1 to $5. Fans have a $15 budget to build their five-player roster.

Players earn fantasy points in categories like points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, and 3-pointers made.

The objective: build a roster that outscores the competition.

In Perfect 5 , fans compete against the broader Yahoo Fantasy community. Those who finish in the top five each week earn points to use in the new Yahoo Sports Shop . In addition, fans can organize private groups to compete directly with friends, or play against likeminded fans in public groups organized by NBA team allegiances. Perfect 5 also features season-long standings to reward fans who build the best rosters week in and week out.

"Perfect 5 adds a new layer of excitement to this season's must-see NBA on Prime broadcasts," Yahoo Sports General Manager Jarrod Schwarz said. "It's a fun format designed to run alongside our season-long games, giving fans more ways to play fantasy basketball on Yahoo and even more reason to watch the NBA on Prime."

The first NBA on Prime doubleheader of the season tips off Friday, Oct. 23, with the defending NBA champion New York Knicks visiting the Boston Celtics, followed by the Houston Rockets taking on the San Antonio Spurs. Fans can start building their Perfect 5 rosters for those matchups now .

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Ja Morant's Expected Blazers Role Ahead of Debut Alongside Damian Lillard
articles.summary: Ja Morant is reportedly expected to be thrust into an unfamiliar role during his first season with the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
Ja Morant is reportedly expected to be thrust into an unfamiliar role during his first season with the Portland Trail Blazers.

According to ESPN Andscape's Marc J. Spears , it is believed Morant will come off the bench for Portland at the start of the 2026-27 campaign, which is something he did only twice in 327 games as a member of the Memphis Grizzlies.

The reason for the change is the fact that the Blazers have a crowded backcourt with Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson on the roster in addition to Morant.

NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season 🫡

Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season 🎯

Portland acquired Morant from Memphis during the offseason at what seemed to be a discounted price, as the Blazers sent Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to the Grizzlies, while including no draft pick compensation.

Originally selected second overall in the 2019 NBA draft out of Murray State, Morant looked like a superstar in the making early in his career.

He was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2020 and Most Improved Player in 2022, and he earned back-to-back All-Star selections in 2022 and 2023.

However, Morant has been limited to a total of just 79 games over the past three seasons combined due to injuries and off-court issues that resulted in multiple suspensions.

Morant's 62 missed games last season were entirely related to injury, as he missed significant time with calf and elbow ailments.

He did manage to average 19.5 points, 8.1 assists and 3.3 rebounds per game when he played last season, and his career averages of 22.4 points, 7.4 assists and 4.6 rebounds per contest are impressive.

For the Blazers, landing Morant felt like a low-risk move since the 27-year-old guard is only under contract for two more seasons.

On top of that, the Blazers have plenty of guard depth in the event that he is injured or ineffective.

Portland was one of the NBA's biggest surprise teams last season, reaching the playoffs as the No. 8 seed in the Western Conference with a 42-40 record.

In addition to returning key players such as Deni Avdija, Donovan Clingan, Toumani Camara, Holiday and Henderson, the Blazers have now added Morant and Lillard to the mix as well.

It remains to be seen how all of the pieces will mesh, but the talent is undoubtedly there to make another run to the playoffs.

Morant's tenure in Portland will begin Wednesday night when the Blazers host the Phoenix Suns in their regular-season opener.

articles.title: Steve Kerr's Look-Alike Reacts to Viral Video, Reveals Fan Thought He Was Warriors HC
articles.summary: Steve Gillis, the recently-discovered doppelgänger of Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr, was able to cash in on his new sort-of-fame by scoring snacks during the team's recent preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Steve Gillis, the recently-discovered doppelgänger of Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr, was able to cash in on his new sort-of-fame by scoring snacks during the team's recent preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers in Las Vegas.

Speaking to Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle , Gillis revealed another fan who was at the game gave him M&Ms, nachos, and beer that she paid for at the concession stand.

"I didn't say anything," Gillis said. "I was so dumbfounded. And she wanted to get the picture, and she wanted to get away. I didn't correct her. I did not. I'm sorry! I did not!"

Evans noted the entire cost of the concession items bought was $46.

Gillis appeared to catch the attention of Kerr during the Oct. 13 preseason contest between the Warriors and Lakers. He was sitting a few rows behind the Golden State bench when Kerr seemed to look in his direction and stop when he noticed.

According to Evans, Gillis said he has been mistaken for Kerr for several years. It has even gotten to a point where his students — he is an English teacher at a Las Vegas-area high school — "come up to him in the halls."

The actual Kerr will lead the Warriors in their season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday night at Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: El Baskonia carga contra Galbiati: "Quería irse al Barça y prescindir de tres jugadores emblemáticos"
articles.standfirst: Félix Fernández, director deportivo del club baskonista, arremete contra el antiguo entrenador en la presentación de Velimir Perasovic
articles.summary: Félix Fernández, director deportivo del club baskonista, arremete contra el antiguo entrenador en la presentación de Velimir Perasovic
articles.body: El nuevo entrenador de Kosner Baskonia, Velimir Perasovic, apuntó este miércoles que le gusta "jugar rápido", y añadió que además quiere que su equipo defienda "con responsabilidad individual y rebotee". El técnico croata negó en rueda de prensa de su presentación oficial las informaciones que salieron en verano que dieron su fichaje por cerrado con el Baskonia y aseguró que los primeros contactos fueron tras el partido de Dubái. "Tengo contactos con amigos con los que hablo, pero oficial no había nada", aclaró. "Tenía que decidir rápido y de verdad no fue fácil porque estaba a punto de irme con mi mujer y tuve que cambiarlo todo en un día", desveló Perasovic que no lo dudó tras la llamada de Baskonia. "Considero mi deber con el Baskonia, porque es el club que me dio la primera oportunidad como entrenador fuerte, es el club que me metió en la rueda de entrenadores de Euroliga, y además lo considero mi club", afirmó el técnico balcánico. "Espero que esta época sea fructífera para los dos y que el equipo pueda enamorar al público de Vitoria. Lo más importante es la disposición de los jugadores, que es buena", deseó el entrenador, en un inicio "precipitado" en su cuarta etapa en el banquillo. "Es evidente que estamos en una época donde todo parece un poco más negro de lo que en realidad es, y creo que con tiempo será más bonito de lo que parece. Tenemos bastante potencial en el futuro para mejorar y dar el baloncesto que queremos", analizó Perasovic, consciente de que ahora tiene "una plantilla bastante corta". "No tengo otro remedio que trabajar con lo que tenemos e intentar aprovechar todo lo que tenemos. Pero para esto necesitas algo más de tiempo y algo más de entrenamientos", expresó el croata, que expuso que "el equipo ha hecho muchas cosas buenas que hay que mantener". Respecto a su plan en el equipo, dijo que va a meter seguro sus sistemas nuevos y en defensa insistirá más "en la responsabilidad individual". "Estas cosas pasan por defender con mucha más responsabilidad, intentar tener más solidez posible, rebotear y tener buen balance defensivo, porque a veces cuando tiras rápido no tienes buen balance defensivo, pero son hábitos que se consiguen trabajando día a día", escudriñó el nuevo técnico azulgrana. Por su parte, el director de Kosner Baskonia, Félix Fernández, adelantó que el equipo busca dos jugadores en el mercado, uno de ellos un 'cinco' y otro que mejore al equipo "en cualquier posición". Además, el dirigente explicó la versión del club sobre el despido de Galbiati: "La decisión se tomó por su mensaje derrotista y las excusas. Detectamos una situación no proactiva de Paolo, con una serie de actuaciones con la secretaría técnica. Quería irse al Barcelona y deseaba prescindir de tres jugadores emblemáticos, entre ellos Sedekerskis. Le explicamos que son elementos sumamente importantes para el proyecto y por su recorrido en el club y que son amados por la afición. Nos pasaba también con otros dos o tres jugadores más".

articles.title: Suns' Mat Ishbia Discusses Kevin Durant Exchange Over Trade After Viral Social Media Posts
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns governor Mat Ishbia says he doesn't "have a problem" with Kevin Durant after a social media argument with the former Suns star.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns governor Mat Ishbia says he doesn't "have a problem" with Kevin Durant after a social media argument with the former Suns star.

The online conversation started Saturday after Durant responded to a recent CNBC Sport interview in which Ishbia described acquiring Durant as part of an initial ownership strategy of throwing "money at the problem."

"I know he didn't watch the video. He might have just read something, and he made a comment," Ishbia told ESPN's Brian Windhorst around the 35:45 mark of Wednesday's episode of Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective.

Ishbia initially said in his CNBC Sport interview he struggled after purchasing the Suns in 2023 to establish team culture, and that without that, even "bringing in super talented players like Kevin Durant doesn't lead to championships."

Durant, who had previously criticized the Suns for the way the franchise ended his tenure in Phoenix, pushed back against the interview in a series of social media posts in which he said the team had "internal problems before I got there."

Ishbia again mentioned his team "identity" when expanding on his comments with Windhorst.

"I didn't do a good job at the beginning when I was an owner. I just kind of put money in and said, 'Let's go do it.' Now I have an identity, alignment all the way through, and we're going to go build," Ishbia said. "Will that work? We're going to find out. But I know the other way didn't work, for sure."

Ishbia concluded, "I don't have a problem with anything he said. But I'm going to make sure... I go out there and say what I believe as well."

The Suns went 85-79 and made one postseason appearance in which the team was swept from the 2024 first round by the Minnesota Timberwolves in Durant's two full seasons with the franchise.

Durant was ultimately traded to the Houston Rockets in July 2025 after two and a half seasons with Phoenix. He will tip off the first season of the two-year extension he signed with the Rockets last October when his team opens the season Wednesday night against Cooper Flagg and the visiting Dallas Mavericks.

articles.title: Knicks superfan Tracy Morgan roasts Bronny James before NBA season opener
articles.summary: Tracy Morgan's brutal Bronny James jab goes viral.
articles.body:
Tracy Morgan delivered an unexpected shot at Bronny James during the New York Knicks ' championship celebration on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The comedian and longtime Knicks superfan criticized the Los Angeles Lakers guard during NBC Sports' pregame coverage at Madison Square Garden.

"Bronny look like he got juco [junior college] ball written all over him," Morgan said. "I just want to say what I feel. What you want?"

The remark caught the broadcast panel off guard, with former Knicks star Carmelo Anthony laughing beside Morgan. The moment soon circulated across social media, drawing mixed reactions from the basketball community.

CBS Sports' Brandon Howard reacted, posting, " This is lame ."

Sports influencer Kristopher London reacted, posting, " You realize how premeditated this comment has to be to even bring it up here? Weird."

Sports content creator Clark wrote, " Atleast Bronny doesn't sound like a… you know what forget it."

Bronny was not involved in the game, but his connection to Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James made the comment particularly notable. LeBron made his debut for Philadelphia after leaving the Lakers during the offseason.

Bronny James' preseason struggles add context

Morgan's comments came after a difficult preseason for the younger James. Bronny struggled with his shooting and averaged just 2.2 points per game. Despite those struggles, the Lakers retained him on their opening-night roster after waiving Dalton Knecht.

The Knicks, meanwhile, entered the season celebrating their first NBA championship in 53 years. Their ceremony included championship rings and the raising of a new banner before Philadelphia spoiled the occasion.

The 76ers secured a 106-100 victory with LeBron scoring 14 points. Tyrese Maxey led Philadelphia with 28 points, while Jaylen Brown added 19.

Morgan's roast became one of the night's most talked-about off-court moments. However, Bronny has an opportunity to respond through his performances as he begins another season with the Lakers.

The comment may have been delivered for laughs, but it renewed questions about Bronny's place in the NBA. His development and opportunities in Los Angeles will remain under scrutiny as the season progresses.

The Lakers open their season at home against the Golden State Warriors at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday on ESPN and the ESPN app.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama reveals 'obvious' reason for Opening Night struggles
articles.summary: Wemby had a horrific shooting night in the Spurs' season opener
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama didn't exactly start the season off hot. The San Antonio Spurs star went 1 of 13 from the field for 12 points in a loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder , coughing up four turnovers as well.

Thunder rookie Aday Mara bothered Wembanyama with his 7-foot-3 frame, but Wemby didn't credit his struggles to any single defender. Instead, he says improvement must come from within.

"I feel like it's obvious for me," Wembanyama said postgame. "I need to go back to playing the basketball I like. This is not the sport I like right here. I got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. For me, it's as simple as that. I'm good when I have fun."

It's possible Wembanyma was a little tight against the Thunder considering the immense expectations the Spurs are facing this season. San Antonio made a surprise NBA Finals run a year ago, falling to the New York Knicks in five games with Wembanyma becoming somewhat of a villain in the process.

Getting back to his fun-loving self could be Wemby's path back to greatness.

articles.title: Where Jayson Tatum, Paul George Landed in Sporting News' NBA Opening Night Winners And Losers
articles.summary: The Celtics' two co-stars had differing starts to their 2026-27 seasons.
articles.body:
Even in a loss, there was a lot to be encouraged about for the Celtics on opening night.

Boston fell to Detroit, 121-113, allowing the Pistons to come back in the second half and spoil an excellent debut for newcomer Paul George. But from an optimistic stance, the new-look Celtics had a strong first half, looked impressive defensively and shot well from deep.

For George and his co-star, Jayson Tatum, it was a fairly different start to the new season, though.

Here's where Tatum and George were placed among the NBA's winners and losers from opening night by The Sporting News.

Jayson Tatum, Paul George Among NBA Opening Night Winners And Losers

Even with the Celtics' blown 22-point lead to the Pistons, their new co-star, George was listed as a winner of the opening slate of games by Sporting News' Steph Noh.

"George was the biggest bright spot," Noh wrote. "Boston was the perfect fit for George on paper, and he proved it in practice."

George finished with 38 points, which set a new Celtics record for points in a team debut. He added five steals, flashing the two-way talent he was known for in the prime of his career.

Tatum, meanwhile, was listed as a loser from the opening games.

"The expectation was that he could fill into Brown's role from last year," Noh wrote of Tatum. "He did playmake for others, recording 11 assists on the day. His shot selection was mostly terrible though, and he was an ugly 6-of-23 from the field."

With Tatum missing all seven of his 3-point attempts, it was a rough shooting night for him against Detroit. He'll be looking to bounce back as the season moves along — the best version of Tatum alongside a resurgent George could make the Celtics title contenders.

Meanwhile, a former Celtic, Jaylen Brown, was listed by Noh as a winner from opening night, as his new 76ers team beat the Knicks, 106-100. Brown, who scored 19 points, "had some good chemistry with LeBron," Noh wrote.

There's a long way to go for both Brown and the 76ers, and Tatum, George and the Celtics in 2026-27. So far, it's looking like a potential win-win deal for Boston and Philadelphia.

articles.title: Escándalo en Grecia: el presidente de la Federación, detenido por presunto amaño de partidos
articles.standfirst: Vangelis Liolios, otros dos directivos y tres árbitros, arrestados en una investigación que mantiene bajo sospecha unos 50 encuentros de todas las categorías del baloncesto heleno
articles.summary: Vangelis Liolios, otros dos directivos y tres árbitros, arrestados en una investigación que mantiene bajo sospecha unos 50 encuentros de todas las categorías del baloncesto heleno
articles.body: Escándalo en el baloncesto griego. Según medios locales, el presidente de la Federación, Vangelis Liolios, y otras cinco personas han sido arrestadas este miércoles en el marco de una investigación llevada a cabo por la Dirección de Crimen Organizado por presuntas violaciones de la legislación deportiva, soborno y amaño de partidos. Los detenidos, además del mencionado Liolios, son dos miembros de la junta directiva de la Federación Griega (EOK) y tres árbitros. Todos ellos se enfrentan a un proceso judicial, dependiendo de su presunta participación en los delitos de corrupción deportiva. Según los informes, los partidos bajo sospecha serían cerca de 50 e incluirían a todas las categorías del baloncesto heleno, desde competiciones de formación y campeonatos escolares hasta la Liga Griega. Entre ellos podría haber incluso uno disputado en el extranjero. Los primeros datarían de 2016 y se extenderían hasta este mismo año. Uno de los hechos que se conoce hasta el momento es el hallazgo de 820.000 euros en efectivo en el domicilio de un árbitro en una zona rural. Los investigadores también habrían encontrado importantes sumas de dinero en posesión de otras personas implicadas, cuyo origen suscita interrogantes. Los expedientes incluyen denuncias y declaraciones de ocho testigos. Dos de los cuales se consideran especialmente importantes debido a su conocimiento de las presuntas actividades de amaño de partidos. De hecho, ellos mismos pudieron ser sobornados en el pasado. Su colaboración en este caso, sin embargo, podría evitarles cualquier condena.
